text:
The passage describes a lighthouse that has been abandoned for decades, its stone weathered and its iron gallery rusted. The keeper's cottage beside it is also old, with a cold stove and a faded tin of tea. The text reflects on the importance of patience and careful measurement, as well as the changing nature of coastal landscapes.

The lighthouse is not a prominent feature anymore, but it serves as a reminder of the past. The shadow of the tower moves with the tide, and the sense of place is maintained even as the surroundings change. The passage emphasizes the value of preserving such landmarks, even when they are no longer used for their original purpose.

The idea of measuring well requires patience and attention to detail. This principle is applied to the maintenance of the lighthouse and the surrounding area. As the harbour silted up, the fishing boats moved to a deeper anchorage, and the cottages were repainted. Only the tower remained, as it was too valuable to be altered.

The passage concludes with a reflection on the usefulness of a landmark: to remain in place long enough that people can measure how far they have traveled from it. This idea is a reminder of the importance of staying true to a place, even as the world changes around us.
